standard.title: First Nations drama
standard.description: explore examples of drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored the arts as important for people and communities (Foundation). They are developing awareness that drama is used across different cultures and contexts (AC9ADR2E01). No specific prior knowledge of First Nations drama is assumed.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore examples of drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians, attending to how elements of drama communicate connection to culture and Country/Place.

nodes.label: When, where and why First Nations Australians use drama
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify occasions when First Nations Australians use drama and explain why drama is important in those contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies at least one occasion (e.g. NAIDOC Week, Sorry Day, Reconciliation Week, community storytelling) when First Nations Australians use drama and gives a simple reason for it.
nodes.typical_width: Students explore when, where, how and why First Nations Australians use drama to share knowledge about their cultures; they investigate drama associated with cultural celebrations and significant occasions using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians.
wider: Students explore how First Nations Australians use drama to express connection to and responsibility for Country/Place — including communicating knowledge about local seasons and sustaining ways of life
Students engage directly or via co-created resources with stories that communicate knowledge of the environment in their region through drama
nodes.hinge_reason: Without understanding why First Nations Australians use drama — its cultural purpose, not just its existence — students observe drama as spectacle rather than as a living cultural practice; the second node about elements and meaning cannot proceed meaningfully.

response_modes.reason: Use resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians to ensure cultural authority; offer varied contexts (celebration, storytelling, ceremony) so students encounter the breadth of purpose.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of First Nations dramatic traditions, cultural occasions and knowledge-sharing contexts across Australia is broad; wider engagement builds richer appreciation of cultural diversity and purpose.
success_criteria: Student names at least one occasion or context when First Nations Australians use drama
Student gives a simple reason why drama is important in that context

nodes.label: How elements of drama communicate in First Nations contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe and describe how elements of drama — place, language, movement — are used in First Nations Australians' cultural expressions they have experienced.
nodes.minimum_width: Student describes one way an element of drama (e.g. movement, language) is used in a First Nations drama example they have observed.
nodes.typical_width: Students observe how elements of drama such as place, language and movement are used in First Nations Australians' cultural expressions; they describe what they notice; they explore how drama communicates knowledge through stories in their region using direct engagement or co-created resources.
wider: Students co-create (as appropriate, with cultural authority and guidance) a Welcome to Country or Acknowledgement of Country to perform before their drama class
Students explore how First Nations drama communicates ways of caring for the land, sea, sky or waterways, connecting drama to environmental knowledge

response_modes.reason: Guide students to name specific elements they observe ('What do you notice about the movement?', 'What is happening with language and voice here?') to make element-level observation explicit.

success_criteria: Student observes and names at least one element of drama used in a First Nations cultural drama example
Student describes what that element communicates or expresses in that context
